We need retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <=9999. Need propose route using templates. We have target: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. Looks like an anilide attached to a triazine? Actually c2nnn... It's a 1,2,4-triazine? The core: c2nnn(Cc3... )c2N attached to carbonyl (amide) linking to an aniline with methoxy.

Potential disconnections:
1) Amide bond formation between aniline (4-methoxy aniline) and carboxylic acid derivative of the heterocycle (e.g., 5-amino-1,2,4-triazine-3-carboxylic acid?). The heterocycle part: c2nnn(Cc3... )c2N with carbonyl attached to N (amide). So we could have carboxylic acid on heterocycle (e.g., 5-amino-1,2,4-triazine-3-carboxylic acid) then couple with aniline.

2) The heterocycle attached to benzyl group bearing p- (CN4CC(F)C4) phenyl. So we could disconnect the C–C bond between triazine carbon and benzyl (C–C bond formation via SNAr? Actually it's a C–C bond formed via alkylation of triazine nitrogen? The triazine has N attached to benzyl? The SMILES: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. The Cc3... is attached to N of triazine? The pattern: nnn(Cc3...) indicates N attached to CH2-aryl. So we could form that via nucleophilic substitution of a halomethyl aryl (e.g., bromomethyl phenyl) with triazine anion.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:
Step1: Amide coupling: target -> aniline (4-methoxy aniline) + heterocycle acid (e.g., 5-amino-1,2,4-triazine-3-carboxylic acid with benzyl substituent). Use standard amide formation (e.g., using EDC/HATU). So leaf: 4-methoxyaniline (commercial) and heterocycle acid.

Step2: Synthesize heterocycle acid: start from 5-amino-1,2,4-triazine-3-carboxylic acid (commercial?) and perform N-alkylation with benzyl bromide (para-substituted with CN4CC(F)C4). So leaf: 5-amino-1,2,4-triazine-3-carboxylic acid (maybe available) and benzyl bromide (or chloride) with side chain.

Check availability: search for "C1=NNN=C1C(=O)O" gave acid (OC(=O)C1=CNN=N1) price $55. That's the heterocycle acid (maybe 1,2,4-triazine-3-carboxylic acid). It has no amino substituent though. Need amino at position 5 (the N attached to benzyl). The acid we have is just the heterocycle with carboxylic acid, no extra N. But our target heterocycle has an exocyclic N (c2nnn...c2N) meaning there is an amino group attached to the triazine ring (maybe at position 5). The acid we have may have that N? The SMILES "OC(=O)C1=CNN=N1" corresponds to 1,2,4-triazine-3-carboxylic acid (no extra amino). The target has an extra N attached to the ring (maybe at position 5). Could be 5-aminotriazine-3-carboxylic acid. Might be commercially available? Search for "NC1=NNN=C1C(=O)O" gave price high $1414 etc. That's the aminotriazine acid (NC1=NNN=C1C(O)=O). That's expensive but still within budget maybe one gram $1414. Acceptable.

Thus leaf: aminotriazine-3-carboxylic acid (price $1414). Good.

Now need benzyl bromide with side chain CN4CC(F)C4. The side chain is a fluorinated azetidine? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a 3-membered? Wait N4CC(F)C4 is a azetidine? N4CC(F)C4 is a four-membered ring with fluorine on carbon. That's a 3-azetidine? It's a 3-membered? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a 3-membered? N-CH2-CH(F)-CH2? It's a 3-membered? Not important.

We need benzyl bromide: c1ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc1 attached to CH2Br? Actually we need a benzyl bromide where the benzyl carbon is attached to the aromatic ring and also to CH2Br (i.e., bromomethyl phenyl). So SMILES: BrCH2c1ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc1. Let's search.
